To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vascular regulation in the Flammer syndrome (a) is a continuum between the normal and pathological state; (b) is characterized by a reduced vasodilation in response to cold and emotional stress; and (c) can be normalized by an adaption of nutrition, in particular by the intake of omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin C, magnesium and vitamin B2.
the FS subjects are characterized by a low BMI, an increased sensitivity to cold and an increased sensitivity to emotional stress.
the FS phenotype is characterized by an altered reaction of blood vessels to coldness, stress, and hypoxia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adaption of nutritional recommendations to the individual health condition of a subject with FS.
a personalized adaption of nutrition to prevent the progression of diseases.
finding the optimal nutritional strategy for subjects with FS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a healthy nutrition for subjects with FS should be a nutrition that is not too low in calories and that does not contain too much salt.
subjects with FS should eat healthy food and avoid unhealthy food.
the nutrition of individuals with FS should be personalized and adapted to their health condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a healthy food consumption for FS subjects should be a balanced nutrition that includes a sufficient amount of carbohydrates, fats and proteins.

subjects with FS should avoid a low-calorie and low-salt diet, but should increase the consumption of fruits, vegetables, fish and nuts, and should reduce the consumption of meat, especially red meat.
subjects with FS should avoid fasting, avoid salt restriction, avoid low calorie diet and avoid low BMI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a preventive nutrition for subjects with FS should be individualized and that a general recommendation of healthy nutrition cannot be applied to all individuals with FS.
a healthy diet for subjects with FS should not be based on the recommendations for a normal population but on the recommendations for subjects with vascular dysregulation.
a healthy diet for subjects with FS is one that is adapted to the individual health condition.
